Strand: WAVES AND OPTICS Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning
Topic 2.1: Properties of Waves
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 24

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Properties of Waves, part of WAVES AND OPTICS Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do you relate waves to the basic properties of light? 2. How Doppler’s effect is applied in real life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Properties of Waves together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: the learner practices the act of exchanging information or expertise on learnt knowledge among

themselves while performing experiments with peers to demonstrate wave properties, sketch wave patterns and make

presentations.

• Self-efficacy: the learn develops leadership skills while ordering and prioritizing tasks as they perform experiments

to demonstrate formation and properties of stationary waves, citing their respective applications and associated

numerical relationships in modes of vibration.

Values

• Social Justice: The learners shows cooperation while according each other equal opportunities in sharing

responsibilities while performing experiments with peers to demonstrate wave properties, sketch wave patterns and

make presentation

• Patriotism: The learner shows dedication by being conscious of their social and moral duties while using print or non- print media to search for information on the behavior of sound waves from an approaching and receding ambulance

or music from moving vehicles and discuss the variations in the frequencies of sound heard to describe Doppler’s

effect.
